We've attached a small log bundle and Grafana screenshots to this message. Can you triage immediately? Voyager is on a tight release window today and this is blocking customer demos.

Sanjay

Subject: Re: Production latency spike + 5% error rate — immediate help needed

Initial triage notes (08:29):
- Grafana shows GPU utilization jump on node pool redwood-pool-12 around 07:47, sustained high KV cache miss rate for the hot prefix.
- Error rate correlates with timeouts from model V2 variant for long-context requests.
- Throughput drop due to request timeouts piling up on the scheduler.

Immediate mitigations in progress:
1) Flushing problematic cache entries and warming prefix cache (in progress, ETA 8–12 minutes).
2) Adding node pool capacity: autoscale request submitted; provisioning logs show new instances requested.
3) Routing: plan to temporarily route long-context traffic to the smaller V1 variant (lower LRU pressure) — need approval from product/ops.

I'll update in 10 minutes. Sharing raw traces in the Drive link.

— Laura
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
attachment: infra-trace-08-29.txt (txt)
From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 08:35:12 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production latency spike + 5% error rate — immediate help needed

Ops update (08:35):
- Autoscale exercised but provisioning lagging in the region (cloud quota slow). We're initiating emergency reroute to a nearby region (us-west-2 -> us-west-1) and enabling burst capacity on Dedicated pool for Voyager (will incur overage).
- Suggested immediate config change: lower max_sequence_length to reduce KV memory pressure for requests originating from voyager-prod-prefix. This is low-risk and reversible.
- I'll coordinate with infra to apply routing and sequence cap; ETA 18 minutes to start seeing improvement.

Vivek
Head of Platform Ops, Redwood Inference
From: markus_klein@redwood.com

Subject: Fwd: War-room invite + exec note

Forwarding calendar invite for visibility. Short executive ask for Voyager: can your execs be available for a 30-min update at 10:30 PDT? They requested an exec-level summary.

Brief for execs (for the invite):
- Impact: increased tail latency (p95->p99) and 5% error rate affecting interactive product flows; user-facing demos degraded.
- Root cause (working hypothesis): KV cache churn + long-context model variant causing scheduler starvation.
- Immediate mitigations: cache warm, route to V1, cap sequence length, burst dedicated pool.
- Risk: temporary cost increase and potential minor quality regression if routed to V1.

Markus
VP, Customer Success, Redwood Inference
attachment: voyager-war-room.ics (calendar invite)
From: jonas_weber@redwood.com
To: Sanjay Patel <sanjay@voyager.ai>, Claire Hughes <claire.hughes@voyager.ai>, markus_klein@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 10:33:40 -07:00
Subject: Status update — Voyager production incident (10:33 PDT)

Sanjay / Claire — quick executive summary for your leadership: 

1) Current state:
- Error rate has dropped from peak 5% -> 1.2% after initial routing and cache warm. Latency tail improving (p95 down ~30%). Throughput recovering to ~87% baseline.

2) What we did:
- Warmed KV prefixes and flushed problematic entries.
- Temporarily routed long-context requests to the V1 variant.
- Enabled burst capacity on Dedicated pool and initiated region failover for affected sub-traffic.

3) Open actions / timeline:
- QA/engineering to validate correctness impact for 2 hours (Marissa + Laura) — target 12:45 PDT to confirm full mitigation.
- Ops will monitor autoscale and finalize node provisioning (Vivek) — expected by 11:00 PDT.
- Postmortem and cost impact report by EOD; we'll share a detailed rollback plan if QA flags quality regressions.

4) Ask of Voyager execs:
- Please confirm whether to keep traffic routing to V1 for the next 2 hours or revert immediately once p95 stabilizes.
- Any objections to short-term burst cost coverage — we recommend Redwood absorb initial minute-by-minute overage and then reconcile.

We'll continue real-time updates in this thread and the war-room.

— Jonas
Director, Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
From: Claire Hughes <claire.hughes@voyager.ai>
